exact_statement: Under iid nearest-neighbor FPP with a<=tau_e<=b, 0<a<b, the uniform centered exponential envelope E exp(alpha |T(0,w)-E T(0,w)|/|w|^q)<=K for every w!=0, and the stated deterministic terminal bias B_n, w381 L1-L5 imply P(D(0,v_n)>sqrt(C L_n(B_n+K0+3s)/(2rho)))<=min(1,A_n K exp(-alpha s/(((C+1)L_n)^q))) along the rounded direction minimizing g on the Euclidean sphere. Here C=(b/a)sqrt(d), K0=bd/2+rho sqrt(d)/2, A_n=2|Lambda_n|+1 and Lambda_n={z:||z||_1<=(b/a)||v_n||_1}.
assumptions: iid undirected nearest-neighbor FPP on Z^d, d>=2
uniform centered exponential moment at scale |w|^q for all nonzero w
proof_or_counterexample: Subadditivity gives b(x)=h(x)-g(x)>=0. Along any minimizing path, T(0,v)=T(0,z)+T(z,v), so the norm excess equals b(v)-b(z)-b(v-z)+X(0,v)-X(0,z)-X(z,v) and is at most b(v)+3s on the centered-envelope event. The Euclidean segment inequality S-L>=2r^2/S holds for interior projections by convexity and for overshoots because S-L>=r and S>=2r. The norm minimum rho and coordinate rounding give norm excess at least 2rho r^2/(CL)-K0. All path vertices lie in deterministic Lambda_n; Markov plus a finite union bound gives the probability. Edge maxima occur at vertices by convexity of distance to the segment along each edge.
remaining_gap: No upper envelope at the conjectured q, no matched global chi_a=chi_b or xi_a=xi_b for one concrete law, and no lower wandering exponent. This is directional only.

exact_statement: For 0<beta<1, h(0)=0 and h(n)=n+n^beta is subadditive with limiting slope one; deterministic T_n=h(n) has every centered exponential bound, yet h(n)-n=n^beta is not O(n^q log n) when q<beta.
proof_or_counterexample: (m+n)^beta<=m^beta+n^beta gives subadditivity; T_n-E T_n=0 identically; n^(beta-q)/log n tends to infinity.
remaining_gap: This scalar deterministic countermodel does not disprove Alexander's FPP-specific nonrandom fluctuation theorem or solve P0110.

exact_statement: For g(s,t)=|s|+|t| and u=(1,0), u minimizes g on the Euclidean unit circle and g(u+(0,t))-g(u)=|t|>=t^2 for |t|<=1, but no local upper bound C t^2 holds at the same direction.
assumptions: g is the l1 norm on R^2
proof_or_counterexample: g(u+(0,t))-g(u)=|t| and the ratio to t^2 equals 1/|t|, which diverges at zero.
remaining_gap: Norm counterexample only; no claim that this is the limit norm of Uniform[1,2] FPP.

exact_statement: For B_n~Bern(n^-1/2), C_n~Bern(n^-1/4), X_n=n^1/2(B_n-n^-1/2), D_n=n^3/4 C_n, the sequence exponential-upper endpoints are chi_a=1/2 and xi_a=3/4, while variance/mean lower endpoints are chi_b=1/4 and xi_b=1/2; hence chi_a=2xi_a-1 despite both endpoint pairs differing.
assumptions: only the one-dimensional marginals stated; no cross-n independence needed
proof_or_counterexample: Var(X_n)=n^1/2(1-n^-1/2), E D_n=n^1/2. The rare B_n=1 and C_n=1 events contribute polynomial probabilities times exp(alpha n^(1/2-s)) and exp(alpha n^(3/4-s)); these diverge below their upper endpoints. Bounded amplitudes prove the matching upper sides.
remaining_gap: Abstract sequence counterexample only, not an iid FPP law or a proof of exponent existence.

exact_statement: If nonnegative D_n satisfy P(D_n>sqrt(U_n+V_n t))<=exp(-t) for all t>=0, with deterministic U_n<=A n^(2tau)log(2+n) and 0<V_n<=B n^(2tau), then for every r>tau and lambda>0 the exponential moments sup_n E exp(lambda D_n/n^r) are finite.
assumptions: full all-t tail, not a single polynomial-probability threshold
proof_or_counterexample: Put Y_n=((D_n-sqrt(U_n))_+)^2/V_n. Its tail is at most exp(-t); layer cake yields E exp(Y_n/2)<=2. Since D_n<=sqrt(U_n)+sqrt(V_nY_n), Young's inequality gives E exp(lambda D_n/n^r)<=2 exp(lambda sqrt(U_n)/n^r+lambda^2 V_n/(2n^(2r))). The right side is uniformly bounded when r>tau.
remaining_gap: Applying w381's input gives only a conditional directional upper wandering endpoint; no global or lower exponent matching.

exact_statement: If nearest-neighbor weights lie in [a,b] with 0<a<=b<3a, every geodesic between neighboring vertices is the direct edge, so D(0,e_1)=0 and the literally printed Auffinger-Damron (2.2) lower wandering infimum over all nonzero v is zero for every exponent.
assumptions: Auffinger-Damron D uses distance to the endpoint segment over all geodesics
proof_or_counterexample: Any alternative path between adjacent lattice vertices has odd length at least three by bipartiteness, hence cost at least 3a>b while the direct edge costs at most b. The unique direct geodesic has zero deviation from its endpoint segment.
remaining_gap: Chatterjee Theorem 1.1 A4 excludes small displacements. This finite obstruction does not address that asymptotic condition or settle P0110.

exact_statement: For iid Uniform[1,2] nearest-neighbor FPP on Z^d, d>=2, let chi_a be Chatterjee Theorem 1.1 upper fluctuation endpoint and g the FPP norm. Choose a Euclidean unit vector u minimizing g(u), and let v_n be coordinate roundings of nu. For every r>(1+chi_a)/2 there exists lambda>0 such that sup_{n>=n0} E exp(lambda D(0,v_n)/n^r)<infinity, where D is maximum deviation of all geodesics from [0,v_n]. This is only a directional upper bound, conditional on the cited published nonrandom-fluctuation theorem and the reviewed peer lemmas; it does not imply a global wandering endpoint.
assumptions: iid Uniform[1,2] on nearest-neighbor Z^d, d>=2
Chatterjee Theorem 1.1 A1 definition of chi_a
w381 L1-L5 and w382 all-t tail upgrade
proof_or_counterexample: For each q>chi_a, A1 supplies K,alpha for w381 L5 at scale |w|^q. Theorem 4.1 supplies B_n<=C n^q log n along v_n. L5 gives P(D>sqrt(U_n+V_n t))<=e^-t with U_n=O(n^(1+q)log n) and V_n=O(n^(1+q)); w382 shows uniform exponential moments at every r>(1+q)/2. For given r>(1+chi_a)/2 choose q in (chi_a,2r-1).
remaining_gap: Independent w386 audit; no global upper or lower wandering endpoint and no matched exponents for P0110.

exact_statement: On a ray with dependent nonstationary bounded positive edge weights tau_j=1+(sigma_j-sigma_(j-1))epsilon, sigma_n=min(sqrt(n)/4,1+dist(n,{4^k:k>=1})/4), the passage times T_n=n+sigma_n epsilon have a uniform exponential upper fluctuation threshold 1/2 and an all-large-n variance lower threshold 0, despite an exact variance-normalized exponential moment exp(alpha).
assumptions: nonstationary edge weights driven by sigma_n
proof_or_counterexample: Both components of sigma_n are 1/4-Lipschitz on nonnegative integers, so tau_j lies in [3/4,5/4]. At n=4^k, k>=2, sigma_n=1; at n=2*4^k, sigma_n=sqrt(n)/4. Also 1/4<=sigma_n<=sqrt(n)/4. Since |T_n-E T_n|=sigma_n, the upper threshold is 1/2; variance=sigma_n^2 and the anchor subsequence makes the lower threshold 0. The normalized moment equals exp(alpha).
remaining_gap: This is not iid, stationary or a Z^d undirected FPP law; it refutes only an abstract shortcut to exponent matching.

exact_statement: For a family T_v with finite positive variance sigma(v)^2, if sup_v E exp(alpha |T_v-E T_v|/sigma(v))<=K and for every eta>0 one has c_eta |v|^(chi-eta)<=sigma(v)<=C_eta |v|^(chi+eta) uniformly for all sufficiently large |v|, then the uniform exponential upper fluctuation endpoint chi_a and the large-distance variance lower endpoint chi_b both equal chi.
assumptions: finite positive variance for every nonzero lattice v
uniform two-sided variance power envelope for every eta>0
proof_or_counterexample: For q>chi choose eta=(q-chi)/2; sigma(v)/|v|^q is bounded globally after handling finitely many small v, so normalized concentration gives the q-scale exponential upper bound. For q<chi choose eta=(chi-q)/2; the lower envelope gives Var T_v/|v|^(2q) bounded below at large v. Any exponential q-upper bound implies Var T_v<=2K|v|^(2q)/alpha_q^2, precluding a variance lower bound at r>q. Thus chi_a<=chi<=chi_b<=chi_a.
remaining_gap: Neither normalized concentration nor uniform two-sided variance power regularity is proved for iid Uniform[1,2]; wandering endpoint matching is untouched.
